title: Plan a studio workflow from a design file to filled templates and a developer handoff
scenario: Your studio plans the launch kit for a café chain. One Figma file holds the approved designs. Canva fills the city posters. Adobe's Firefly API makes the wide banners. The app developers get the promo card. You plan each step before work starts. Use the exhibit. The brand, the files, the people and the numbers are made up for this case. The vendor lines are copied from the docs.
exhibit:
BRIEF (made up):
  Tidewell Café opens in 30 cities on 1 June. Launch kit:
  30 city posters, 3 wide web banners, and a new promo card in the app.

DESIGN FILE (made up):
  Figma file "Tidewell Launch". The PromoCard component uses the
  colour variable brand/sea-500 and the shared Button component.
  Developer's first plan: paste a PNG of the card into an AI chat and
  ask it to "build this card in React".

TEMPLATES (made up):
  Canva brand template "City poster", fields CITY, DATE, PHOTO.
  The Lisbon poster is approved and already printed.
  A teammate wants to refill that same Lisbon design with Porto data,
  using autofill-design with update_in_place.

BANNERS (made up):
  Source: cup_hero.png (square). The cup and its logo must not change.
  Plan: Firefly Fill to replace the background, then Expand to 3:1.

SCHEDULE (made up):
  The client wants a script to read the Figma file every Monday at
  06:00 and list any layer that uses a raw hex colour. Nobody is online.

HANDOFF (made up):
  Studio plan: Figma Organization, developers on Dev seats.
  The developers want the AI agent to use the real PromoCard and
  Button components, not new ones.

VENDOR LINES (copied from the docs):
  OpenAI vision: "The model doesn't process original file names or metadata."
  Canva autofill-design: "update_in_place replaces the existing design's content and can't be undone"
  Adobe masks: "Black areas are protected." "White areas are exposed."
  Figma plugins: "It's not possible to build plugins that run in the background."
  Figma Code Connect: "Available on a Dev or Full seat on the Organization, and Enterprise plans"

questions.prompt: The developer plans to build the PromoCard from a pasted PNG. What do you ask for instead?

options.text: A larger PNG at twice the size, so the model can read the exact colour token names
options.explanation: A bigger picture still holds only pixels. The token name is in the file, not the image.

options.text: Design context and variables from the file, with the screenshot only to check the look
options.explanation: Right. Figma's tools return the variables and structure, and the screenshot helps layout fidelity. A PNG alone carries no token names.

options.text: Nothing else, because a vision model reads the layer names that are saved in the PNG
options.explanation: OpenAI says the model doesn't process original file names or metadata.

options.text: A PDF export of the whole page, because PDFs always keep the variable names inside
options.explanation: No cited page says this. Ask the design server for variables and design context.

questions.prompt: The teammate wants to refill the printed Lisbon design with Porto data, using update_in_place. What do you say?

options.text: Fine, because Canva keeps a copy of the old poster and can undo it any time later
options.explanation: Canva says update_in_place replaces the content and can't be undone.

options.text: Fine, because update_in_place makes a new design and leaves Lisbon as it was before
options.explanation: It does the opposite: it replaces the existing design's content.

options.text: Don't, since it replaces Lisbon for good; make Porto a new design from the template
options.explanation: Right. Canva says to set update_in_place only when the user explicitly asks to refill that design. Nobody asked to lose Lisbon.

options.text: Don't, because autofill-design can only write text, and the Porto photo is an image
options.explanation: Canva lists image as a template field type, and its own example fills a hero photo.

questions.prompt: For the Fill step on cup_hero.png, how should the Firefly mask be painted?

options.text: Cup and logo white, background black, so the edit focuses on the cup
options.explanation: White areas are exposed to edits. This would change the cup and keep the old background.

options.text: Everything white, because Fill finds the background by itself from the prompt
options.explanation: A fully white mask exposes the whole image, cup and logo included.

options.text: Everything black, because black tells Firefly where the new background goes
options.explanation: Black areas are protected. Nothing would change.

options.text: Cup and logo black, background white, so only the background can change
options.explanation: Right. Adobe says black areas are protected and white areas are exposed.

questions.prompt: Where should the Monday 06:00 colour check live?

options.text: A REST API script on a schedule, because Figma need not be open for it to run
options.explanation: Right. Figma's comparison page says scheduled scripts use the REST API, with no user present.

options.text: A Figma plugin that the studio sets to start by itself every Monday morning
options.explanation: Figma says it's not possible to build plugins that run in the background.

options.text: A widget on the canvas, which checks the file each time a person refreshes it
options.explanation: A widget needs someone to view or refresh the file. Nobody is online at 06:00.

options.text: A Dev Mode plugin, since Dev Mode plugins are the ones allowed to run on a timer
options.explanation: Figma says Dev Mode plugins are read-only and for inspection and codegen. No timer is described.

questions.prompt: How do you make the AI agent use the real PromoCard and Button components?

options.text: Wait for an Enterprise plan, because Code Connect is not on Organization plans
options.explanation: Figma says Code Connect is available on a Dev or Full seat on Organization and Enterprise plans.

options.text: Connect both with Code Connect, so the server sends the real imports and snippets
options.explanation: Right. With Code Connect, the MCP server adds CodeConnectSnippet wrappers with import statements and component snippets.

options.text: Export both components as SVG files, so the agent can copy the code from the SVG
options.explanation: An export is a picture of the layer. It does not tell the agent which code component to use.

options.text: Rename both layers in Figma, because the agent finds the code by matching names
options.explanation: Clear names help, but Figma says the server won't know your conventions without Code Connect, variables or prompts.
